23684-keats-poems-published-in-1820.title: Keats Poems Published In 1820
23684-keats-poems-published-in-1820.creator: Unknown
23684-keats-poems-published-in-1820.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Of all the great poets of the early nineteenth century--Wordsworth, Coleridge, Scott, Byron, Shelley, Keats--John Keats was the last born and the first to die. The length of his life was not one-third that of Wordsworth, who was born twenty-five years before him and outlived him by twenty-nine.

arxiv-2110-11950.creator: Adel Javanmard, Mohammad Mehrabi
arxiv-2110-11950.description: Abstract Over the past few years, several adversarial training methods have been proposed to improve the robustness of machine learning models against adversarial perturbations in the input. Despite remarkable progress in this regard, adversarial training is often observed to drop the standard test accuracy. This phenomenon has intrigued the research community to investigate the potential tradeoff between standard accuracy (a.k.

arxiv-2212-01002.title: Automatic Depth-Optimized Quantum Circuit Synthesis for Diagonal Unitary Matrices with Asymptotically Optimal Gate Count
arxiv-2212-01002.creator: Shihao Zhang, Kai Huang, and Lvzhou Li
arxiv-2212-01002.description: Abstract Current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices can only execute small circuits with shallow depth, as they are still constrained by the presence of noise: quantum gates have error rates and quantum states are fragile due to decoherence. Hence, it is of great importance to optimize the depth/gate-count when designing quantum circuits for specific tasks.

arxiv-2212-09378.title: Special families of piecewise linear iterated function systems
arxiv-2212-09378.creator: R. Dániel Prokaj, Károly Simon
arxiv-2212-09378.description: Abstract . This paper investigates the dimension theory of some families of continuous piecewise linear iterated function systems. For one family, we show that the Hausdorff dimension of the attractor is equal to the exponential growth rate obtained from the most natural covering system.

arxiv-2302-04911.title: PoS(LATTICE2022)412 ADP-23-04/T1214 DESY-23-017 Liverpool LTH 1331 Quasi-degenerate baryon energy states, the Feynman–Hellmann theorem and transition matrix elements
arxiv-2302-04911.creator: J. M. Zanotti
arxiv-2302-04911.description: Abstract The standard method for determining matrix elements in lattice QCD requires the computation of three-point correlation functions. This has the disadvantage of requiring two large time separations: one between the hadron source and operator and the other from the operator to the hadron sink.

arxiv-2304-04690.title: Digraph Colouring and Arc-Connectivity
arxiv-2304-04690.creator: Pierre Aboulker, Guillaume Aubian, Pierre Charbit
arxiv-2304-04690.description: Abstract The dichromatic number χ → ⁡ ( D ) \dic(D) of a digraph D D is the minimum size of a partition of its vertices into acyclic induced subgraphs. We denote by λ ⁡ ( D ) \lambda(D) the maximum local arc connectivity of a digraph D D .

arxiv-2307-00969.title: High Altitude Platform Stations: the New Network Energy Efficiency Enabler in the 6G Era Thanks: This research was supported by the Generalitat Valenciana, Spain, through the CIDEGENT PlaGenT, Grant CIDEXG/2022/17, Project iTENTE.
arxiv-2307-00969.creator: Tailai Song 1 , David Lopez 3 , Michela Meo 1 , Nicola Piovesan 2 , Daniela Renga 1
arxiv-2307-00969.description: Abstract The rapidly evolving communication landscape, with the advent of 6G technology, brings new challenges to the design and operation of wireless networks. One of the key concerns is the energy efficiency of the Radio Access Network (RAN), as the exponential growth in wireless traffic demands increasingly higher energy consumption.

arxiv-2310-10450.title: Quantum Error Channels in High Energetic Photonic Systems
arxiv-2310-10450.creator: B. C. Hiesmayr, W. Krzemień, M. Bała
arxiv-2310-10450.description: Abstract In medical applications –such as positron emission tomography (PET)– 511 511 keV photons that experience Compton scattering are studied. We present a consistent framework based on error-correction channels to fully describe the quantum information-theoretic content of high energetic photons undergoing Compton scattering, characterized by the Klein-Nishina formula in unoriented matter.

arxiv-2411-04941.title: Internal Solitary Wave Generation Using A Jet-Array Wavemaker
arxiv-2411-04941.creator: Jen-Ping Chu, Patrick Lynett, Mitul Luhar
arxiv-2411-04941.description: Abstract This paper evaluates the experimental generation of internal solitary waves (ISWs) in a miscible two-layer system with a free surface using a jet-array wavemaker (JAW). Unlike traditional gate-release experiments, the JAW system generates ISWs by forcing a prescribed vertical distribution of mass flux.

arxiv-2503-16968.title: Modelling Material Injection Into Porous Structures Under Non-isothermal Conditions
arxiv-2503-16968.creator: J.-S. L. Völter, Z. Trivedi, A. Boger, T. Ricken, O. Röhrle
arxiv-2503-16968.description: Abstract In this work, the Theory of Porous Media (TPM) is employed to model percutaneous vertebroplasty, a medical procedure in which acrylic cement is injected into cancellous vertebral bone. Previously, isothermal macroscale models have been derived to describe this material injection and the arising mechanical interactions.

pmc-11379442.title: GoBot Go! Using a Custom Assistive Robot to Promote Physical Activity in Children
pmc-11379442.creator: Rafael Morales Mayoral, Ameer Helmi, Samuel W. Logan, Naomi T. Fitter
pmc-11379442.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Children worldwide are becoming increasingly inactive, leading to significant wellness challenges. Initial findings from our research team indicate that robots could potentially provide a more effective approach (compared to other age-appropriate toys) for encouraging physical activity in children.

pmc-11388802.title: The relationship between the lifestyle health index and voter turnout during the 2020 United States presidential election in the context of regional cultures
pmc-11388802.creator: Ross Arena, Nicolaas P Pronk, Thomas E Kottke, Anthony Arena, Colin Woodard
pmc-11388802.description: ObjectivesThere are numerous population health challenges confronting the United States (U.S.), including the unhealthy lifestyle – chronic disease pandemics. However, the impact of unhealthy lifestyle behaviors and the increased prevalence of chronic diseases that result from them affect many facets of life outside of the health domain, and their scope remains under-appreciated.

pmc-11477878.title: A Flexible Multifunctional Sensor Based on an AgNW@ZnONR Composite Material
pmc-11477878.creator: Hao Lv, Xue Qi, Yuxin Wang, Yang Ye, Peike Wang, Ao Yin, Jingjing Luo, Zhongqi Ren, Haipeng Liu, Suzhu Yu, Jun Wei
pmc-11477878.description: A multifunctional sensor comprising flexible and transparent ultraviolet (UV) photodetectors (PDs) with strain gauges based on Ag nanowire (AgNW)@ZnO nanorods (ZnONRs) was fabricated using a cost-effective, simple, and efficient method. High-aspect ratio silver nanowires were synthesized using the polyol method. An AgNW@ZnONR composite was formed via the hydrothermal method to ensure the multifunctional capability of the flexible sensors.

pmc-11571079.title: Evaluation of Klebsiella pneumoniae pathogenicity through holistic gene content analysis
pmc-11571079.creator: Miyu Isogai, Kumiko Kawamura, Tetsuya Yagi, Shizuo Kayama, Motoyuki Sugai, Yohei Doi, Masahiro Suzuki
pmc-11571079.description: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative bacterium that causes both community- and healthcare-associated infections. Although various virulence factors and highly pathogenic phenotypes have been reported, the pathogenicity of K. pneumoniae is still not fully understood. In this study, we utilized whole-genome sequencing data of 168 clinical K. pneumoniae strains to assess pathogenicity.

pmc-11656990.title: Evaluation of N-NOSE as a surveillance tool for recurrence in gastric and esophageal cancers: a prospective cohort study
pmc-11656990.creator: Sayuri Iitaka, Akihiro Kuroda, Tomonori Narita, Hideyuki Hatakeyama, Masayo Morishita, Umbhorn Ungkulpasvich, Takaaki Hirotsu, Eric di Luccio, Koichi Yagi, Yasuyuki Seto
pmc-11656990.description: ObjectiveEarly detection of recurrent gastric and esophageal cancers remains a critical challenge. Innovative and non-invasive cancer screening technologies, such as N-NOSE, can improve early detection. N-NOSE is a urine-based scent test that leverages the olfactory abilities of the nematode C. elegans.

pmc-11698369.title: A novel recommender framework with chatbot to stratify heart attack risk
pmc-11698369.creator: Tursun Wali, Almat Bolatbekov, Ehesan Maimaitijiang, Dilbar Salman, Yasin Mamatjan
pmc-11698369.description: Cardiovascular diseases are a major cause of mortality and morbidity. Fast detection of life-threatening emergency events and an earlier start of the therapy would save many lives and reduce successive disabilities. Understanding the specific risk factors associated with heart attack and the degree of association is crucial in the clinical diagnosis.

pmc-12570729.title: Interaction effect of age and axial length-to-corneal radius ratio on myopia in children and adolescents: a cross-sectional study in China
pmc-12570729.creator: Jingfeng Mu, Haoxi Zhong, Huimin Zhu, Mingjie Jiang
pmc-12570729.description: BackgroundMyopia has emerged as a significant public health concern in China. Despite age and axial length-to-corneal radius ratio (AL/CR) being widely recognized as independent factors influencing myopia in children and adolescents, very few studies have investigated the combined effects of these two factors or the extent of their interaction.

pmc-13680928.title: Fully Threaded Versus Partially Threaded Cannulated Screws in the Treatment of Nondisplaced or Valgus-Impacted Geriatric Femoral Neck Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13680928.creator: Mark Ayoub, Samuel Saucedo, Emilio Robles, Yeng Vue, Armen Martirosian
pmc-13680928.description: Introduction:Partially threaded cannulated screws (PTCS) have been associated with high rates of femoral neck shortening (FNSH) and complications in the treatment of geriatric femoral neck fractures. There are limited studies directly comparing the use of all fully threaded cannulated screws (FTCS) with PTCS. The purpose of this study was to compare outcomes between FTCS versus PTCS.
